WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (term_premium_lapse_and_conversion), revision 2 after the policy-task audit.
[Step 0 draw] prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[6,4,4,4]: grace remittance 6; conversion, waiver ending and face decrease 4 each.
[Why a good test] Harold asks only to have his approved face decrease put through. The decrease is recorded only while in force ('The installment after the face decrease is not recorded until the policy status on record has moved from the grace period back to in force.') and the record shows grace_period after the 2026-06-15 draft came back. The decrease releases premium from the installment on record, which must first be right: the bank-draft privilege ended with the second eft return, so the installment is converted to quarterly direct billing (456.39), and the waiver rider expired at the 2026-07-15 anniversary (age 65), so its charge comes out of that converted installment (401.32). Harold's own remittance (577.23) cures the grace period; it counts the 2026-07-15 installment at the quarterly mode without the waiver charge, the overdue 2026-06-15 installment from the ledger, and one returned-item charge. Every premium write is read by a later scored write: the conversion by the waiver ending, the waiver ending by the decrease, and all of them land in the remittance or the final installment.
[Scope] claims term_ext_eft_quarterly_conversion, term_ext_waiver_expiry_repricing, term_ext_grace_cure_remittance, term_ext_face_decrease_repricing; tools convert_to_quarterly_billing_2bfb08af, end_expired_waiver_rider_bcdc46e8, remit_grace_premium_a5ae3e41 (owner=user), apply_face_decrease_78b62126. Task 1 holds the lapse/reinstatement/accidental death/advance policies; scopes disjoint.
[Problem-tree card] root term_ext_face_decrease_repricing; edges: decrease<-remittance state_gate (term_face_decrease.decrease_status); decrease<-waiver ending value_input (record_installment); remittance<-conversion value_input (mode_factor); remittance<-waiver ending value_input (waiver_charge); waiver ending<-conversion value_input (record_installment). Each sentence is a state-form sentence with an ordering connective, verbatim in the blocked rule; exactly one write in the difficulty brings each state about (premium_mode quarterly: conversion; rider flag false: waiver ending; grace->in force: the remittance). Deletion runs (executed): skip conversion -> waiver ending 132.73, remittance 308.42; skip waiver ending -> remittance 632.30, decrease 279.59; skip remittance -> status stays grace_period. Order is unique (chain).
[Base-invariant card] mode_change_status, rider_change_status, payable_status: status grace_period at handling time; cure_within_grace: paid-to 2026-06-15 + 31 days (OH) = 2026-07-16, frozen_time is the inclusive last day; decrease_status: in force after step 12; policy year 21, no decrease this policy year, 240,000 >= 100,000.
[Business-object card] policy LT10462835; decrease request (new face 240,000); ledger: 15 billed installments 2025-04-15..2026-06-15 at 150.91, 18 remittances, 4 returns (2025-05-20 eft, outside 12 months; 2025-11-20 eft; 2026-02-19 check; 2026-06-22 eft). Whole life WL10288514 in force (550,000) counts toward the band and the fee share; the Ashgrove Protection UL UL10385517 lapsed in 2019 and counts toward neither (near-miss for band and fee share in every computation, the waiver ending included).

user_scenario: You are Harold J. Whitcombe, 65, a retired high-school shop teacher in Columbus, Ohio, who owns an Ashgrove Level Term 25 policy on his own life. You speak plainly and a little gruffly, in short sentences, and you dislike being transferred. You are calling because a few weeks ago you mailed Ashgrove a signed form to lower your term coverage to $240,000, and you got a letter saying the request was approved; you want the coverage lowered now so the premium comes down. Open with something like: "I sent in a form to lower my coverage on my term policy and I want it put through today." You do not know your policy number by heart and say you would rather they look it up. You give your telephone number, 6145550137, when the representative first asks who you are. Only when asked to confirm your identity do you give, one at a time as asked, your date of birth, 1961-04-08, the last four of your Social Security number, 1846, and your ZIP code, 43220. If asked what amount you asked for on the form, you say $240,000. If asked whether you hold other policies with Ashgrove, you say you also have a whole life policy with them that you still pay on, and an old universal life policy you let go years ago. You have no idea what your premium is now or what it will be after the change; you never offer a figure and never guess one. Only if the representative tells you that a payment is needed before the change can go through, you agree right away and say you will pay it by debit card yourself; when the representative hands the payment step over to you, you make the payment of exactly the amount the representative names, by debit card, and read back the confirmation you receive. If the representative tells you the way your premiums are billed or charged has to change, or that a rider has come off the policy, you accept it without argument, saying something like "Fine, if that's how the contract works." If the representative quotes a figure and asks whether it looks right, you say you can't check it yourself and trust them to have it right from your records. Once the representative tells you the lower coverage has been recorded and gives you the new premium, you say thanks and end the call.

edges.policy_source: The released premium is taken from the installment on record only after that installment no longer carries the charge of a waiver rider whose insured's anniversary age has reached the waiver rider expiry age.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The order is fully fixed by the prerequisite sentences: the waiver ending takes its charge out of the converted installment on record, so it follows the conversion; the remittance follows both (quarterly mode, rider detached); the decrease follows the remittance (in force) and releases premium from the installment the waiver ending left. No two writes are unordered.

Skipping the waiver ending leaves 456.39 on record: the decrease records 279.59 instead of 224.52, the rider stays attached, and the remittance becomes 632.30.
Skipping the conversion leaves monthly_eft on record: the newly due installment is priced at 0.0875 and the remittance falls from 577.23 to 308.42.
Skipping the waiver ending keeps the 207.82 waiver charge in the newly due installment: remittance 632.30 instead of 577.23.
Skipping the conversion leaves the monthly installment 150.91 on record: the waiver ending computes 132.73 (150.91 less 207.82 x 0.0875) instead of 401.32.
